/-!
# Erdős Problem 453

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/453](https://www.erdosproblems.com/453)
- [Er70b] Erdős, P., *Some applications of graph theory to number theory*. Proc. Second Chapel Hill
  Conf. on Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Univ. North Carolina, Chapel Hill, N.C.,
  1970) (1970), 136-145.
- [Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory day
  (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
- [Po79] Pomerance, Carl, *The prime number graph*. Math. Comp. (1979), 399-408.
-/

namespace Erdos453

/-- The eventual prime inequality asked in Erdős Problem 453, using Mathlib's zero-based primes. -/
def EventuallyHasPrimeWitness : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
    ∃ i : ℕ, i < n ∧
      (Nat.nth Nat.Prime n) ^ (2 : ℕ) <
        Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n + i) * Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n - i)

/--
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $i<n$ such that
$$
p_n^2 < p_{n+i}p_{n-i},
$$
where $p_k$ is the $k$th prime?

Pomerance proved that the answer is no.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos453.lean"]
theorem erdos_453 : answer(False) ↔ EventuallyHasPrimeWitness := by
  sorry

end Erdos453

findings.description: The [Er74b] reference names “Remarks on some problems in number theory,” pp. 197–202, but the prime question occurs in the separately titled “Problems,” pp. 203–204. These two items are bundled in the same archive PDF. This is a bibliographic slip, not an error in either Lean declaration.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf: after the preceding article ends on p. 202, p. 203 starts “4.33. (1974) 203–204 PROBLEMS.” Item 4.33.2(I), headed “Problem of P. Erdős and Straus,” asks about infinitely many primes satisfying the reverse prime-product inequality for every positive i < k. The problem website also locates its [Er74b] reference on p. 203.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace or clarify this reference to cite Erdős, P., “Problems,” Math. Balkanica 4 (1974), 203–204, specifically Problem 4.33.2(I).

reformulations.difference: With q_n = Nat.nth Nat.Prime n = p_{n+1}, literal reindexing of the source permits 0 < i ≤ n. The file instead permits i < n, without an explicit positivity condition. The predicates differ at some small individual indices, but their eventual assertions are equivalent.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The case i = 0 can never witness the strict inequality, since it gives q_n² < q_n². The only remaining difference is i = n, whose product is 2q_{2n}. Standard prime-growth estimates imply q_k = o(k²), while q_n ≥ n + 2; consequently 2q_{2n} ≤ q_n² for all sufficiently large n. Thus the omitted endpoint eventually cannot witness the inequality. Reindexing the center by one and enlarging the threshold then gives precisely the source’s assertion. A full equivalence was proved as ReviewIndex453.actual_iff_source in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, using prime-growth lemmas rather than either version of the problem’s solution. Its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in either declaration. The negative answer, research solved category, and external formal-proof record agree with the source. Scratch checks verified the answer’s scope, prime enumeration, safe subtraction, exclusion of i = 0, and small examples. The linked external proof also compiled with only standard axioms after four local, statement-preserving compatibility edits for the sandbox’s newer Mathlib. Full text of Er77c and the full Gu04 A14 page could not be accessed; their available metadata/snippets were checked, and the other primary sources suffice to settle both declarations. All experiments and proof adaptations are under /workspace/review; no repository files were edited.
